title: AI Safety & Money: What Never to Share With a Chatbot
guestBio: Stephanie Guttman is the Cofounder & CEO of Huntress Wealth, an AI-powered financial independence platform built for women+. She also leads Guttman Development Partners, a commercial real estate development firm, and cohosts the podcast Talk Rich to Me. With a finance background and an MBA, Stephanie believes every woman has the power to take control of her financial future — no finance degree required.
excerpt: What if the free AI tool you're using to manage your money is quietly training on every detail you share? Stephanie Guttman, Cofounder & CEO of Huntress Wealth, is back on The Manage Her® to lay out the AI privacy rules she lives by — and the financial data you should never, ever upload. This one will make you rethink every chatbot conversation you've had about money.
metaDescription: Stephanie Guttman of Huntress Wealth shares AI safety rules for women — what never to upload, how to diversify AI tools, and how to protect your financial data.
keyTakeaways: Free AI tools typically train on your data, so you should assume that anything you type into a no-cost chatbot is not fully private.
Never input financial account details, medical records, government IDs, passwords, your children's information, or client data into an AI tool.
Diversify the AI tools you use across different areas of your life so that no single platform can build a complete profile of who you are.
Before trusting any financial professional with your money, verify their credentials and fiduciary status on the SEC and FINRA public databases.
Insurance is a legitimate and important piece of a healthy financial plan, but it is never a substitute for an actual investment vehicle.
A business pivot is not a failure when your core mission remains intact — only the method of delivering on it has changed.
Money doesn't transform your character; it amplifies whatever you already are, which makes building the right mindset before wealth arrives essential.

pullQuotes.text: If you're not paying for it, you are the product. That rule doesn't stop at social media — it applies to every free AI tool you've ever opened.
I just want to make women really rich. That's it. That's the whole mission.
Money doesn't change you. It amplifies you — the good and the bad. So get right with yourself before the money arrives.
Fiduciary is my F-word. Ask every financial professional whether they are one before you hand them a single dollar.
I diversify my AI tools the same way I diversify a portfolio. No single system gets to hold the full picture of my life.

quiz.title: What's Your Money & AI Personality Type?
quiz.description: How you handle money and technology says a lot about your instincts, your boundaries, and where your biggest growth edge lives. Answer these six questions honestly — there are no wrong answers — and discover which financial archetype fits you best right now.

A.name: The Protective Planner
A.description: You are the woman who reads the terms of service. You don't hand over information until you understand exactly where it's going, and you hold that same careful energy around your financial life. Your superpower is discernment — you don't get swept up in hype. Your growth edge is learning to move forward confidently even before you have every answer, because perfect information rarely exists. In this episode, Stephanie's Never-Share List will feel like validation, and her framework for diversifying AI tools will give your planning instincts a concrete system to work with.

B.name: The Bold Rebuilder
B.description: You have pivoted before — maybe more than once — and you've learned to stop apologizing for it. You move toward opportunity with energy, and you're not afraid to tear up a plan that isn't working. Your superpower is adaptability and vision. Your growth edge is building the protective habits and privacy boundaries that keep your bold moves sustainable over time. Stephanie's story of rebuilding Huntress Wealth from the ground up will feel like a mirror, and her practical AI safety rules will give your boldness the guardrails it deserves.

C.name: The Curious Learner
C.description: You are genuinely excited about AI, about money, about what's possible — and you absorb information quickly. You might already be using several AI tools without having thought too deeply yet about the data you're sharing. Your superpower is openness and momentum. Your growth edge is moving from enthusiastic user to intentional strategist — someone who asks not just what a tool can do, but what it does with you. This episode will sharpen your instincts without dimming your excitement, and Stephanie's portfolio approach to AI will give you a smarter framework to explore.

D.name: The Quiet Powerhouse
D.description: You have been doing the work — financially, professionally, personally — without necessarily broadcasting it. You may feel behind on AI, uncertain about who to trust with your money, or quietly overwhelmed by how fast everything is moving. Your superpower is depth and steadiness. Your growth edge is giving yourself permission to claim the expertise you've earned and to take up more space in conversations about wealth. This episode was made for you. Stephanie's direct, no-jargon approach to both AI safety and financial independence will meet you exactly where you are and remind you that it is never too late to step into your financial power.

questions.question: A friend recommends a free AI tool that can analyze your spending habits. What's your first instinct?

options.text: Research who built it, read the privacy policy, and decide if the trade-off is worth it.
Try it immediately — you can always adjust your approach once you see how it works.
Google every review you can find and then excitedly test it out.

options.text: I have a plan and I protect it carefully — my financial information is mine to guard.

options.text: Analyze the data thoroughly before making any moves — you want to be sure before you shift.
Pivot with conviction — if the mission still holds, the method can always change.

options.text: Ask them directly if they are a fiduciary and then verify their credentials on FINRA before the conversation goes further.
Ask bold, direct questions on the spot and trust your gut about whether they're the real deal.

options.text: Selectively and intentionally — I've thought carefully about what I share and with which platform.

options.text: My careful, protective instincts — I'd build serious security for myself and my family.

content:
There is a conversation happening in every corner of the internet right now about how AI can help you manage your money — budget smarter, track spending, plan for retirement. And almost none of that conversation includes the part where someone tells you exactly what you should never type into that chatbot. That's the conversation Stephanie Guttman came back to The Manage Her® to have.

Stephanie is the Cofounder & CEO of Huntress Wealth, an AI-powered financial independence platform built specifically for women+. She first joined the show when Huntress looked completely different — a membership model built around live sessions. She's back because she tore up that roadmap when the world shifted underneath it, and what she rebuilt is sharper, more accessible, and more needed than ever. If you've been quietly wondering whether it's too late to reinvent yourself or your business, this episode is going to give you permission you didn't know you were waiting for.

A Pivot Is Not a Failure — Here's the Difference

One of the most quietly powerful moments in this conversation comes early, when Stephanie talks about the decision to dismantle her original business model and build something new. She's clear-eyed about it in a way that most founders never let themselves be publicly: the method changed, but the mission never did. Her North Star — making women financially independent — held firm. Everything else was just the vehicle, and vehicles can be upgraded.

If you have ever felt the pull to change direction in your business or career and feared what others would call it, Stephanie's reframe is worth sitting with. Evolution looks like failure from the outside when the observer doesn't know what you're actually optimizing for. You do. Trust that.

The F-Word Every Woman Should Know Before Hiring a Financial Professional

Stephanie calls fiduciary her F-word — and she means it as the highest compliment. A fiduciary is legally required to act in your best financial interest, not theirs. Not every financial professional is one. Not every advisor you've ever met was one. And most women were never told to ask.

Before you hand any professional access to your money, ask them directly: are you a fiduciary? Then verify their credentials yourself on the SEC and FINRA public databases — both are free and take minutes. Stephanie also flags a red flag worth memorizing: when an insurance product gets positioned to you as an investment, that is a signal to slow down and ask more questions. Insurance has a real and important role in your financial picture. It is not, however, a replacement for investing.

If You're Not Paying for It, You Are the Product

This is the line that will rewire how you think about AI tools forever. The rule most people know from social media applies with equal force to every free chatbot you've opened: if you are not the paying customer, your data is the revenue model. Free AI tools generally train on user inputs. What you type in may not stay private. That matters enormously when the topic is your financial life.

Stephanie doesn't say avoid AI. She uses it, she loves it, she built her company around it. What she does instead is treat AI tools with the same strategic thinking she applies to a financial portfolio — she diversifies. Different tools for different parts of her life. No single platform gets to hold a complete picture of who she is, what she earns, what she owns, or where she lives. That's not paranoia. That's portfolio management applied to your digital identity.

The Never-Share List: What Stays Off Every Chatbot

Stephanie is specific, and specific is what makes this actually useful. Here is what she will never input into an AI tool, free or paid: financial account numbers and banking details, credit card information, medical records, government-issued IDs, passwords, her children's personal information, and any client or confidential professional data. She draws the line clearly and she doesn't apologize for it.

You don't have to give a tool your full financial picture for it to be useful. You can ask conceptual questions, explore scenarios, and learn frameworks without handing over the raw data of your actual life. That boundary is yours to hold, and this episode will help you hold it with confidence instead of guilt.

Why Women Reach Retirement With Less — And What to Do About It

The financial gap women face at retirement isn't accidental. It's the compounded result of wage gaps, career interruptions, longer life expectancy, and — critically — a financial services industry that was not designed with women as the primary client. Stephanie built Huntress Wealth specifically to close that gap, because she believes financial independence isn't a luxury for women. It's protection, freedom, and power.

The episode goes deep on why AI — when used correctly and safely — is one of the most democratizing tools women have ever had access to. Stephanie calls it the best thing for women since the washing machine. Not because it replaces human judgment, but because it removes the gatekeeping. You no longer need a finance degree or an expensive advisor to start asking better questions about your own money.

Money Doesn't Change You. It Amplifies You.

This is the truth that Aimee and Stephanie keep circling back to, and it's worth letting land. The version of you that arrives at financial independence will be a louder, more resourced version of who you already are today. If you are generous now, you will be more generous. If you are anxious now, more money will surface more anxiety — until you do the inner work.

That's not a reason to delay building wealth. It's a reason to build the relationship with yourself alongside it. The mindset work and the money work aren't separate tracks. They're the same track, and this episode treats them that way.

Whether you're just beginning to take your finances seriously, rethinking how you use AI in your daily life, or in the middle of a business pivot that scares you a little — this conversation with Stephanie Guttman is exactly where you need to be right now. Press play. Your future self will thank you for not skipping this one.
